answers.text: I'm a final-year mechanical engineering student in Dehradun. I hold the NCC 'C' certificate with grade B, and as Senior Under Officer I led a drill squad of 30 cadets. My final-year project is a low-cost solar water heater prototype that reached 55 degrees Celsius in four hours. I also spent three weeks at an auto-components plant. I want an MBA because I found that production decisions are as much about people and cost as machines.
NCC has taught me discipline, leadership and national integration. I believe in leading from the front and I will bring the same spirit to my MBA and to my career.

The hardest thing as Senior Under Officer was that the 30 cadets were from very different years. Some of them arrived late for the 5:30 a.m. drill. I started a rule that late cadets did the opening drill, and the lateness stopped in a month.
Do you follow motorsport? I watched the last race with my friends, and I think the pit-stop strategy was the real story. It is quite similar to plant operations, in a way.
I can't describe the plant's rejection rates or the customer names from my internship. They told us not to share production data outside the plant.
